additional_777_readings.own_independent_semantic_note: The complete Arabic chain ends with Abdullah said, and the whole substantive exhortation and first-person observations are his statement in this field. It does not contain a Messenger-said link. Keep all source words and the internal honorific, actual observations and conditions; do not supply a missing Prophetic attribution from the Hindi/Urdu/Roman siblings.

The complete English field expressly says Abdullah said. Keep this Companion statement and its first-person observations, source grammatical defect I have a man coming, and the unclosed ending exactly. The Day-of-Judgment, daily and of-worshippers parentheses are explicit explanatory glosses. Do not import the Hindi/Urdu/Roman Messenger-said attribution or silently complete punctuation.

The complete Roman Urdu field explicitly prints Rasool Allah ne farmaya, followed by your-Prophet and first-person plural observations without an announced voice reset. Preserve this own-source attribution and internal voice ambiguity, visibly marking the difference from Arabic/English. The parenthetic Prophetic-era clarification is context; no canonical correction or missing narrator return is supplied.

records.reading_note: Anas describes the breathless arrival, actual dhikr, Prophet inquiry and twelve angels. Keep the supplied Urdu prayer translation and the parenthetical said-it predicate in the man reply. Humayd supplies an actual additional instruction to walk normally and complete missed rakahs, which needs its own transmitted-addition component; the transmitter introduction is context, not a new eyewitness. The calmness lexical expansion is explanatory context. Preserve all main and addition wording without importing variants.

Both full fields report estimated prayer-standing lengths, with the thirty-verse/Sajdah measure and the successive halves. Retain estimation wording and the surah identity as part of the supplied measure. Hindi is visibly Latin transliteration throughout, so its script needs a visible Latn source-script correction while language/version/source bytes remain unchanged; no Devanagari rewriting.

AbuHurayrah reports the Prophet instruction to announce the Fatiha and another surah condition. Both fields contain a complete finite instruction; preserve the exact statement without a new legal conclusion.

Hakam ibn Araj describes IbnAbbas at Zamzam, the calendar question, ninth-day answer and explicit confirmation of Prophetic practice. Keep the affirmative same-way parenthesis as part of the actual reply and preserve the source number/date, without reconciling it against755.

Main IbnAbbas report gives the Prophet tenth-day instruction. After the compiler grading/disagreement discussion the source supplies an actual separately attributed IbnAbbas saying to fast ninth and tenth and oppose the Jews; retain that finite Companion saying as a separate component. The surrounding compiler grade, unnamed views, footnote and school-alignment remarks remain context. Preserve Hindi damaged school names and do not invent a chain.

AbuHurayrah reports three specific commitments: witr before sleep, three monthly fasts and duha. Keep all three numbered clauses; the salat-alduha parenthetic synonym is lexical context, not an added ritual instruction.

AbuQatadah main dialogue gives the no-fasting/no-breaking reply to perpetual fasting. The parenthetic whole-year gloss and Urdu marker are context; preserve the reported negation. The long compiler discussion mostly gives grades, parallels and legal opinions. Near its end Ahmad and Ishaq explicitly attribute the five-day fasting prohibition to the Prophet; assess that finite attributed summary as a distinct source-supplied report fragment with these later scholars as transmitters, not an invented direct chain. The following not-obligatory-to-break inference remains compiler context.

Abdullah ibn Shaqiq asks Aisha: successive fasting/nonfasting and no full month other than Ramadan are all finite own-source testimony. Keep all those clauses; stop before ImamTirmidhi grading and bare parallel listing. Urdu footnote remains context.

Anas reports variable fasting and night prayer/sleep. Keep the observer phrases we-thought and whenever-you-wished-to-see, which prevent an absolute continuous-fasting reading. Only the final compiler grade is context.

AbuSaid reports the two named Eid fasting prohibitions. Parenthetic Eid synonyms are explanatory context. The subsequent compiler grade, parallel lists, legal practice and narrator biography/transmitter list are not additional narration bodies.

IbnAbbas explicitly reports cupping while in ihram and fasting; keep both simultaneous source qualifications. The subsequent grade, same-report chain comparison and missing-IbnAbbas transmission discussion remain source context, without repairing that chain.

Aisha describes her own delayed Ramadan makeups in Shaban until the Prophet death. This is Companion practice with a temporal limit, not an invented Prophetic command. Only the final compiler grade is outside the report.

Aisha reports the menstruation/purification sequence and the instruction to make up fasts but not prayers. Keep the opposite instructions together. Final grade, alternate-chain pointer and scholarly practice/legal-consensus discussion remain context.

Laqit asks about wudu; preserve the complete instruction and its actual fasting exception. Urdu own nasal-action wording is not corrected from Hindi. The compiler grade and subsequent legal consequence/opinion and bare corroboration remain context.

Zirr asks Ubay about the27th night. Hindi has a damaged shortened answer and no explicit Prophetic attribution; do not import the Urdu heard-from-the-Prophet link. Urdu retains its explicit report and counting/remembering. The later parenthetic Zirr-says marker changes the actual speaker to his own IbnMasud knowledge assertion, so preserve that attribution in its own component. Ray and Muslim-audience parenthetic glosses and final grade are context. No missing Hindi words are supplied.

Uyaynah ibn AbdurRahman transmits his father: AbuBakrah explains his last-ten-night search by a heard Prophetic instruction naming nine/seven/five/three remaining. The subsequent finite account of AbuBakrah ordinary first20-day prayer and greater last-ten effort is a separately attributed Companion-practice observation. Parenthetic month-completion gloss and final compiler grade are context; no calendar harmonization.

Salamah ibn alAkwa narrates revelation, their own fidyah practice and later abrogation as his historical account. Retain the actual verse and full supplied translation, including the Hindi parenthetical translation. Explicit Baqarah184 locator, Urdu footnote markers and final compiler grade remain context; no independent legal ruling is made.

Muhammad ibn Kab describes visiting Anas in Ramadan with journey preparations complete, Anas eating, affirmative sunnah answer and subsequent mounting. This is the actual Companion-practice observation, not direct Prophetic speech. All text is finite narration.

The alternate transmission contains its own finite Muhammad ibn Kab visit to Anas in Ramadan before the same-way pointer. Retain that actually supplied short historical visit without importing799 meal/journey details. The same-way pointer, compiler grading/biography and legal travel discussion remain context.

AbuDharr main Ramadan-prayer report preserves all supplied remaining-night counts, the actual imam-following promise, household summons and fear of missing falah. Hindi printed27th-night English ordinal stays exact. Explicit taraweeh/tahajjud glosses are context, but Urdu would-be-better proposal qualification stays. The closing transmitter what-is-falah/sahri exchange is lexical explanation. Urdu alone then has long compiler legal discussion: within it Shafii explicitly says he observed20-rakah practice in his city Mecca, an actual attributed historical observation to consider separately from surrounding legal preferences, grades, bare parallels and uncertain views. No such tail is supplied into Hindi.

AbuShurayh gives his actually heard Mecca speech to Amr. Hindi ends after the instruction to relay it; do not import the Urdu later exchange. Urdu additionally narrates the troop-dispatch setting and Amr own answer about fugitives, requiring distinct actual attribution rather than Prophetic speech. Keep the speech temporal permission limit and necessary object/scope wording; the war-in-Mecca parenthesis is meaningful to its stated prohibition. The explanatory IbnZubayr identity, combat synonym and rebel gloss require individual context decisions. Compiler grade, biography, bare parallels, wording comparison and legal etymology are context.

Ali describes the hajj obligation revelation, repeated annual question, response and subsequent warning verse. Hindi is damaged and omits part of the conditional; keep its finite own wording without borrowing the fuller Urdu answer. Urdu parenthetical obligatory/yearly wording is the actual question/conditional scope and should stay. Both supplied verse meanings belong to the narrated event. Only Urdu continues into compiler grading, narrator biography and bare parallels, which remain context.

Jabir reports intention, public announcement, gathering, travel to Bayda and ihram. The walking-from-there parenthesis is a supplied narrative movement clause, unlike the Urdu Madinah location gloss. Preserve the actual event and source variation. The Urdu footnote and final compiler grade/parallel list remain context.

IbnUmar challenges the Bayda attribution and gives a talbiyah location. Hindi drops the oath, mosque and explicit repeated Prophet subject supplied by Urdu; do not restore them. The parenthetic allegation-content and DhulHulayfah location are necessary to the own-language claim and especially the damaged Hindi location syntax, so keep these scope/identity elements. Retain Urdu explicit oath and subject, leaving only numeric markers and compiler grade as context. No external harmonization with817.

IbnAbbas attributes tamattu to the Prophet and three named caliphs, then names Muawiyah as first prohibitor. Preserve these distinct historical roles in the classification and exact source claim, without an external ruling or correction. Urdu three numeric markers and final compiler grade remain context.

Abdullah ibn Amr reports mosque trading and poetry prohibition. Keep the nonreligious parenthesis: it restricts the source poetry clause, and deleting it would silently broaden the supplied prohibition. Urdu footnote remains context; no independent legal/authenticity claim is made.

AbuDharr asks about first mosque, next mosque and interval, receiving the own-source forty-year answer and earth-as-prayer-place instruction. Both fields are complete finite dialogue. Only Urdu footnote is context; no outside historical reconstruction.

AbuHurayrah reports an unnamed blind Ansari request for a prayer-place boundary in his house and the Prophet fulfilling it. Keep the reason and actual action; do not supply Itban or another identity. Urdu footnote is context.
Aisha reports the instruction for neighbourhood mosques to be built, cleaned and perfumed. Both complete fields contain actual instructions and no separate explanatory apparatus.

records.reading_note: IbnMasud source explicitly introduces Prophetic speech, then gives obligations, your-Prophet language, a first-person we-used-to-see passage and the walking merit clause without marking a speaker reset. Preserve all actual wording and qualify the unmarked voice in metadata rather than silently repairing it into a different canonical attribution. The explicitly parenthetic Prophetic-era explanation and Urdu marker are context; all actual observations and conditions stay.

Anas describes BanuSalamah proposed move, the Prophet concern about Madinah becoming empty, the footsteps-reward question and their staying. Both complete fields are finite historical narration and contain no separate apparatus.

Abdullah ibn UmmMaktum describes age, blindness, distance and lack of suitable guide, then asks for a concession and answers the adhan question. The congregation-absence parenthesis states the scope of the requested concession and should remain. Keep all actual conditions and replies; only the Urdu numeric footnote is context.

Abdullah ibn Amr reports Maghrib, departing and remaining people, the Prophet breathless arrival with knees visible, and the stated one-door opening and angel address. Preserve the nested divine-address quotation within this reported saying without creating a Quran source or changing one door to all doors. Urdu footnote is context.

IbnMasud describes his left hand above his right and the Prophet physically moving his right hand above his left. Keep both directions/actions and the Urdu lack of final punctuation. No new prayer rule is added.

The unnamed son of Abdullah ibn Mughaffal first describes his father aversion to innovation, then the father hears the recitation and admonishes him, reporting what he himself did not hear while praying with the Prophet and three caliphs. Preserve that not-heard limit rather than an absolute never-said claim, the actual incipits and the aloud predicate including the parenthetic voice word. The son observation and father testimony should be correctly attributed; no son name or unprinted chain is supplied.

Amrah transmits Ziyad letter to Aisha quoting an IbnAbbas claim, asking for a reply and describing his own sent sacrifice. Aisha then explicitly rejects that claim using her own experience making garlands and the Prophet dispatch with her father. Preserve separate letter/claim and Aisha response attributions, all negations and the until-slaughter limit; do not treat the initial claim as an endorsed rule. Hindi sacrificial-animal synonym is context; no unnamed father identity is inserted.

AbdurRahman ibn Harmalah transmits an unnamed man question to Said ibn alMusayyib and his affirmative answer with explicit Prophetic umrah-before-hajj attribution. This finite Successor answer/report needs no invented direct-hearing claim; both own fields are complete.

IbnAbbas reports Fadl riding, reciprocal looking, the Prophet turning Fadl face, the Khatham woman old-father question and yes answer, and the farewell-hajj timing. Preserve the own Urdu tribal spelling, exact disability and proxy question, and final actual timing; no external identity repair or family detail.

Yahya through Malik and IbnShihab attributes a finite historical-purpose statement about the Hatim boundary to an unnamed learned person. It claims the enclosure was made to direct tawaf around the original Kaaba: assess as a numbered attributed historical statement, not Prophetic speech or a bare chain. The speaker remains unidentified; no canonical identity is invented. Parenthetic Hijr synonym is source explanation; preserve the reported exclusive purpose and action.
